'''Ramanujan Srinivasan''' (1938–1984) was an Indian physicist, known for his research on magnetic resonance phenomena.<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee">{{Cite web |url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/Detail.aspx?AID=335 |title=Brief Profile of the Awardee |date=2017 |publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize |access-date=November 12, 2016}}</ref> Using new techniques developed for the purpose, he studied [[ferroelectricity]] which established the significance of [[hydrogen atoms]] and [[ammonium ion]]s in the system.<ref name="Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners">{{cite web | url=http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | title=Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research | date=1999}}</ref> His studies have been documented by way of a number of articles and the article repository of the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] has listed 40 of them.<ref name="Browse by Fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://repository.ias.ac.in/view/fellows/Srinivasan=3ARamanujam=3A=3A.html |title=Browse by Fellow |date=2017 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences}}</ref> He was a fellow of the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="Fellow profile">{{Cite web |url=http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Srinivasan,_Dr_Ramanujan |title=Fellow profile |date=2017 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences}}</ref> The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]], the apex agency of the Government of India for scientific research, awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], one of the highest Indian science awards, for his contributions to Physical Sciences in 1981.<ref name="View Bhatnagar Awardees">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/AwardeeList.aspx | title=View Bhatnagar Awardees | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize | date=2016 | access-date=November 12, 2016}}</ref>{{Refn|group=note|Long link - please select award year to see details}} Srinivasan died on 10 September 1984, at the age of 46.<ref name="Fellow profile" />
